newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-WHITE CALLED UP BY ENGLAND AS COVER FOR IRANI.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WHITE CALLED UP BY ENGLAND AS COVER FOR IRANI.

text.p: Yorkshire all-rounder Craig White has been called up to join the England tour of Zimbabwe.
White is being flown in as cover for Ronnie Irani who has been advised to rest for four days because of a back injury which troubled him during the four- day match against Matabeleland.

White, who made a significant contribution to the England A side's successful Australian tour, will join the senior squad on December 23 in time to be considered for the second test which begins on Boxing Day.
A decision on whether to send Irani home has been deferred. His non- availability further undermines England's options for the first test against Zimbabwe starting on Wednesday.
With Alec Stewart expected to keep wicket rather than Jack Russell, the final place in the side is likely to go to either Andy Caddick or Phil Tufnell.
The pitch at Queen's Club is likely to favour the spinners so Tufnell should play. Caddick has not bowled to his potential on tour.

Zimbabwe have made two changes to the side that beat England by two wickets in Sunday's first one-day international. Opening batsman Stuart Carlisle comes in for all-rounder Craig Evans and fast bowler Henry Olonga replaces medium pacer John Renie.
Off-spinner Andy Whittall has been left out of the 12, while tobacco farmer Andy "Bundu" Waller makes his test debut at the age of 37 after top-scoring with 48 on Sunday.
Zimbabwe - Alistair Campbell (captain), Grant Flower, Stuart Carlisle, Andy Waller, Dave Houghton, Andy Flower, Guy Whittall, Paul Strang, Heath Streak, Eddo Brandes, Henry Olonga.
England (probable) - Mike Atherton (captain), Nick Knight, Alec Stewart, Graham Thorpe, Nasser Hussain, John Crawley, Robert Croft, Darren Gough, Alan Mullally, Chris Silverwood, Phil Tufnell.
